Summary: The seventh commandment: marriage is exclusive, and sexual faithfulness guards the covenant between husband and wife.
Commandment: Do not be unfaithful to your marriage; keep sexual union within marriage alone.
Application: Jesus extends the commandment to the heart: lustful intent already breaks it. The positive side is faithfulness that protects both spouse and family.
Purpose: To guard marriage exclusivity; Jesus roots marriage in creation: what God joined, man must not separate (Matthew 19:4-6).
Function: Marriage is exclusive, and this seventh of the Ten Words guards it. It is foundational moral law, traditionally classed moral, binding in every age. Its goal was faithfulness that protects both spouse and family, rooted by Jesus in creation: what God joined, man must not separate. The evil it addressed was unfaithfulness — breaking the marriage covenant, and in Jesus' extension, lustful intent that breaks it in the heart. It restrained that evil by fencing sexual union inside marriage alone.
